code.originalText: Prenatal visit at 11 weeks: nausea and vomiting review and cell-free DNA screening

text.paragraph: Review at 11 weeks, nine days after discharge from an admission for hyperemesis gravidarum. [S]

Ms. Brontë returns at 11 weeks 1 day. After the sick visit she was admitted for three nights for intravenous saline with potassium, thiamine, magnesium, ondansetron, and enoxaparin, and went home nine days ago keeping down fluids, food, and tablets. She takes ondansetron 4 mg every 8 hours, doxylamine-pyridoxine four tablets a day, and thiamine 100 mg three times a day. She now vomits once a day or less and eats five small meals a day. Her PUQE-24 score is 9. She has mild constipation since starting ondansetron, which she manages with fluids, prunes, and oat bran. She has had no headache, palpitations, pain, or bleeding. She felt low and frightened in the hospital and is now more hopeful. The planned electrolyte check within a week of discharge was not done; blood was drawn today. [S]

text.paragraph: Vital signs recorded on 1855-02-10; see the Vital Signs section. [S]

tr.td: Soft and non-tender; uterus just palpable above the pubic bone
Fetal heart heard by handheld Doppler at 158 per minute
First pregnancy at 38 (elderly primigravida), single live intrauterine pregnancy dated by ultrasound at 7 weeks 1 day
S — Synthetic modern prenatal care anchored to the documented report that she was pregnant when she died; the pregnancy itself is questioned in one source (CLM-0019).
Nausea and vomiting of pregnancy, moderate (PUQE-24 score 10), with early weight loss, under evaluation for hyperemesis gravidarum

S — Synthetic presenting concern at the index visit, superseded by the hyperemesis gravidarum diagnosis at the sick visit; her documented "perpetual nausea" is D and the hyperemesis reading of it is R.

Hyperemesis gravidarum with metabolic disturbance: unable to keep fluids down, 7.4 percent weight loss, dehydration, hypokalemia, hyponatremia, hypochloremic alkalosis, low magnesium, and raised transaminases; PUQE-24 score 14
S — Synthetic modern diagnosis linked to her documented final illness and the retrospective hyperemesis interpretation; it is not asserted as her historical diagnosis.
Gestational transient thyrotoxicosis: suppressed TSH and mildly raised free T4 with hyperemesis, no goiter, eye signs, or tremor; no treatment needed
S — Synthetic finding that teaches the thyroid tests in hyperemesis; it echoes no documented illness.

list.item:
Hyperemesis gravidarum, improving (O21.1). PUQE-24 score 9, down from 14; weight 43.6 kg, up 1.0 kg from the sick visit. Sodium 137, potassium 4.0, chloride 101, bicarbonate 25 mmol/L, urea nitrogen 9, creatinine 0.55, glucose 82, magnesium 1.9, and phosphate 3.4 mg/dL: normal, with no fall in phosphate after refeeding. ALT 31 and AST 24 U/L are back to normal. The post-discharge electrolyte check was late; today's results show no harm. [S]
Continue ondansetron 4 mg every 8 hours, doxylamine-pyridoxine four tablets a day, and thiamine 100 mg three times a day until she eats regular meals.
Constipation: fluids, fiber, and prunes; an osmotic laxative if needed.
No thromboprophylaxis now: age over 35 is her only persisting risk factor; reassess at 28 weeks and at any admission.

Gestational transient thyrotoxicosis (O99.281). No palpitations or tremor; pulse 86. [S]
Repeat TSH and free T4 at 16 to 18 weeks.

First pregnancy at 38 (O09.519). Fetal heart 158 per minute. EPDS 9 with item 10 scored 0: below the threshold, with understandable distress after the admission. [S]
Cell-free DNA screening drawn today.
Nuchal translucency scan in two weeks.
Offered the clinic's perinatal support group and a counselor; she will join the support group.
